prerequisites.reason: Understanding how neurons produce outputs is foundational to understanding neural network behavior and design.
Backpropagation is a training algorithm specifically defined on neural network architectures and requires prior understanding of them.
Backpropagation depends on differentiating neuron output functions, so understanding activation functions is necessary first.
Transfer learning commonly builds on pretrained neural network models, so understanding neural networks is necessary before learning it.
Many core generative modeling approaches in modern machine learning are based on neural networks, making them foundational.
To analyze prediction errors, one must first understand the classification task and outputs being evaluated.
